comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @Morhaus and @vvo to be potential reviewers

To give some more context: while defining the API, we made a lot of hypothesis (bad). One of them was that MAYBE some users would want to set defaultRefinements while letting the user unselect them.

This is an anti pattern. If you want some default refinements while letting the user unselect them then you just link to color=White, yes the default refinement will be present in the url but no big deal.

The main usage (never seen any other usage) of default Refinement being: "I want to preselect this value, and not show the underlying widget, and not have the url being updated with the default refinement".

If a user still wants to show the underlying widget, then it's his responsibility to not allow unselecting default refinements. Maybe we could enforce that ourself in our default widgets.

Hi @mthuret
 why the example here:
https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/react/examples/tourism/index.html
still present in the url with empty value

Hello @terranboy, 

Between the 21 of October and today, we changed our way to provide url synchronisation. Today, if you want to have it, you need to build it yourself because we figured it out that we will never be able to cover all the possible use cases. You can find more information about this on our [dedicated url routing guide](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/react/guide/Routing.html).

So the reason why empty values are still there on the tourism example is that because the implementation we made for the url synchronisation of our examples after removing it from react-instantsearch doesn't handle them. 

Hope this help :)
